You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like June 2010. The unemployment rate is 9.5%, which matches June 2010. Industrial production is up 7.7% year over year, and the 10-year yield is 2.54%, which is low for that period. US equities fell 6.6% in the month, which fits the May–June 2010 selloff tied to the European debt crisis. The VIX at 27 also fits.

Headline CPI of 1.31% and core CPI of 0.98% are consistent with mid-2010. Payroll growth over the three months averaged only 26.67k, which fits June 2010, when census hiring was reversing.

The 10-year yield looks more like end of June 2010, when it was about 2.9%, so I checked the alternatives. The 10-year was about 3.3% at the end of May and about 2.5% at the end of August. The 1-month equity loss of 6.6% would fit May 2010 (about -7.9%), and August 2010 was about -4.5%. June 2010 was about -5.2%.

With a 10-year of 2.54% and a 3-month change of -0.77 against 3.3% at the end of May, the snapshot may be August 2010 instead. Unemployment was 9.5% in July 2010 and 9.6% in August. The 12-month equity return of +4.8% fits August 2010 (August 2009 to August 2010 was about +4.9%). The 20y+ Treasury gain of 9.9% in one month is large, though, and fits a shift like May 2010 or August 2010.

Payrolls over the three months average 26.67k. For data published by end of August 2010, the July report gave unemployment of 9.5%, and payrolls for May–July were roughly 26k on revised figures, so August 2010 fits.
